entry_state: Amendment and debt discharge have separate legal conditions. Cumulative hedge measurements determine reserve changes, with basis adjustment distinguished from recycling and cash settlement. Fair-value hedges and benchmark changes retain their own rules. The excluded-component section now introduces option time value as protection cost; its event and valuation requirements continue next.
exit_state: Option premium, intrinsic gains and related protection cost are separate. Actual strike and designated risk determine different calculations; cumulative component reserves preserve mismatch reversals and hypothetical options create no cash or asset. The next subsection has introduced a zero-cost collar with purchased call and written put, whose gross premiums offset; its valuation continues next.
findings: The option example carries the premium into inventory cost and reconciles cash and equity; omitting it would overstate profit by six.
Time-period amortisation and transaction basis adjustment are distinguished. The lower-initial-time-value example keeps cumulative losses and their later reversal.
The aligned-option equations define prices, quantities and initial values, restrict the cumulative-loss branches and explain the matched-value case. They do not claim a general signed-value selector.
A deliberately wrong hedged strike still balances the books, demonstrating why accounting equality alone cannot establish the correct risk measurement. No new confirmed local defect.
